chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Mismaʿ ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said:
Rasul Allah (عليه السلام) said: Indeed, a servant may be detained on account of a sin from among his sins for a hundred years, while he looks at his wives in Paradise enjoying themselves.

key_terms.أَزْوَاجِهِ: his wives; his spouses in Paradise
key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise; the abode of divine reward
key_terms.الْعَبْدَ: the servant; the human being in relation to Allah
key_terms.ذَنْبٍ: a sin; an act of disobedience for which one is held accountable
key_terms.ذُنُوبِهِ: his sins; the servant’s wrongful deeds
key_terms.مِائَةَ عَامٍ: one hundred years; a prolonged period of detention
key_terms.يَتَنَعَّمْنَ: enjoying blessings; living in delight and comfort

ai.seo_question: How can a sin delay a servant from entering the blessings of Paradise?
ai.summary: This hadith warns that a believer may be delayed from full reward in the Hereafter because of a sin he committed. It emphasizes the grave consequences of sins and the reality of reckoning, even while Paradise and its blessings are within sight.
